options_far.hardware: Prolyte H30V, 4 x H30V-L300 = 12 m span (18.9 kg per 3 m: 75.6 kg), on two H30V towers on base plates with outriggers, top corner blocks; cubes on half-couplers + safety under the bottom chords at 6.6 m
options_far.load_check: 3 cubes x 3.7 kg (LASEROS-MK2) + 3 x 1.0 kg clamps and safeties + 6 kg cable = 20.1 kg as 3 point loads near the third points. Prolyte H30V loading table, 12 m single span: 448.7 kg centre point load, 340.6 kg per point at third points (DIN basis; x 0.85 for BS 7905-2 / ANSI E1.2: 289.5 kg). 20.1 kg is 7 % of it. Towers, base plates and outriggers: the rental house's tower data and a stability check (ANSI E1.21 / EN 13814 class) are owed.
options_far.sources: Prolyte H30V standard lengths (repo: moxir-2026-10-17-minimal-cut-movers.json); H30V loading table (paperclip.rcs.ac.uk HV30_Loading.pdf and H30v-loadingtable.pdf, read 2026-10-08; to be checked against the current Prolyte data sheet)

colour_note: LaserCube Ultra MK2, per colour (scripts/place/fixtures/fixtures.json lasercube.specs.variants_mw, the maker's ULTRA MK2 Guide spec tables): 10 W unit 455 nm 5000 mW, 525 nm 2800 mW, 638 nm 2800 mW; 6 W unit 2700 / 1500 / 1800 mW; 4 mm beam, 1 mrad, Class 4. 'Ash white' = all three diodes at once (a grey-white whose tint depends on the mix; the three beams overlap only as well as the cube's convergence, which the datasheet does not give: colour fringes possible). 'Ember red' = the 638 nm diode alone (deep red); an orange ember needs red + a little green, a mix. The owner's cubes are taken as the 10 W unit: NOT confirmed (a photo of a cube's label is on today's shot list).

haze.source: moxir-versions-2026-10-17.json looksWhy: 'the room is written at sigma 0.02/m (realism.mjs --scattering 0.02, fog far ~80 m) ... from the club-haze research (0.004-0.02)'; the joint sigma call is still owed
haze.g_basis: ASSUMED: Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry for a glycol/oil haze of ~1 um droplets (strongly forward scattering); not measured

advice: Mirror pairs (his video 3: mirrored, one colour per part): 1 and 3 mirror each other about the DJ's axis (ash white); 4 and 5 mirror each other (ember red); 2 sits in the middle in ember red; 6 frames the DJ in ash white.

Every beam toward the stage ends on the near crane's BACK girder (z 19.55-20.25, 7.95-8.75 m): a steel beam stop the hall already has, right behind the DJ. Its face looks away from the crowd, so a mirror-like bounce goes back into the dark far half, not over the dance floor.
Heights: the beams run at 6.5-8.35 m, under the far crane where it stays, over the press, and rise only 1-2 m over 60 m: from the floor they read as near-level lines converging on the stage.
Chase (far to near, a fire burning toward the stage): 2 alone -> 1 + 3 -> 4 + 5 into the side spans -> 6 last, framing the DJ -> all, then black. One colour per part.
4 and 5 show the building: one beam of each crosses its side span and lands on that span's far runway girder, so the span's own columns stand in the line, lit edge-on through the smoke.

palette.key: MOXIR = moxir, ash: the remains of a fire. Ash grey-white light, an ember red-orange glow, smoke, and light rising out of a burnt-out factory: the hall read as what is left after the fire.
palette.lasers: ash white (1, 3, 6) and ember red (2, 4, 5): what the cubes can honestly make (see colour_note)
palette.washes_why: roof pools ash white (the cold underside of a burnt roof), the columns and the far walls ember red-orange (what still glows at the base): RGBW PARs and the HK1915 mix both; the UP-250BSW reaches orange only through its colour wheel (its slots are not in the repo: ASSUMED one is orange/red).

maker_warning: The maker's own manual (ULTRA MK2 Guide): lasers for display or entertainment should be Class 1, 2 or visible-beam 3R; the Ultra MK2 is Class 4, and a Class 4 show needs a laser safety officer and the local permit (fixtures.json lasercube.specs.laser_class).
